description: Design specification for the Java execution infrastructure added in SBG v5, enabling cross-language behavioral genome extraction.

motivation.problem: The SBG project has 10 Python programs with Java equivalents specified in benchmark/cross_language/ (p01–p10), but no actual Java source files or Java execution pipeline exists.
motivation.goal: Enable extraction of DynamicGenome-compatible behavioral signatures from Java programs using the same feature schema as the Python tracer, so Python and Java programs can be compared by distance().
motivation.constraint: No third-party Java parsing libraries. No bytecode instrumentation (ASM/Javassist). Must work with JDK 17 at /usr/bin/javac and stdlib subprocess only.

components.name: JavaInstrumenter
components.role: Inject System.err.println trace calls at method ENTER/EXIT boundaries using string-level regex manipulation. Detects pre-instrumented sources and skips re-injection.

instrumentation_protocol.depth_counter: static int callDepth on the class, incremented at ENTER, decremented in finally block
instrumentation_protocol.why_stderr: Keeps trace output cleanly separated from functional stdout; subprocess(stderr=PIPE) captures them independently

components.name: JavaExecutor
components.role: Orchestrate instrument → javac compile → java run → genome extraction pipeline.
components.graceful_degradation: If /usr/bin/javac is absent, run() returns {status: NOT_AVAILABLE, reason: javac not found} without raising.

components.name: JavaTraceEvent
components.role: Dataclass for a single parsed trace event (mirrors Python TraceEvent structure).

genome_schema.note: All keys mirror DynamicGenome.to_dict() so the existing distance() function works without modification.

keys.coverage_size: int — count of unique (depth_bucket × 1000 + anon_idx) tuples across all traces; structural analogue of line coverage
keys.coverage_consistency: float [0,1] — mean pairwise Jaccard of per-trace coverage sets
keys.anon_call_freq: Dict[str,float] — normalized call frequency keyed by first-call-order integer index (str-keyed to match to_dict() serialisation)
keys.hot_path_hash: str — 16-hex SHA-256 of top-5 anonymous indices by frequency; rename-invariant
keys.exception_type_set: List[str] — sorted unique Java exception class names; no messages (SAFEGUARD-2)
keys.exception_rate: float [0,1] — fraction of input traces that raised an exception
keys.call_depth_mean: float — mean max call depth across traces
keys.trace_length_mean: float — mean event count per trace
keys.trace_length_std: float — std of event count per trace
keys.n_unique_functions: int — count of distinct instrumented methods called

anonymization.rationale: main() is the entry harness, not an algorithm. Constructors and static initialisers carry no algorithmic trace signal. java.* are JDK internals.

coverage_proxy.problem: Java execution traces carry no source line numbers — only method ENTER/EXIT events.
coverage_proxy.solution: Synthetic coverage token = depth_bucket * 1000 + anon_method_index. Two ENTER events at the same method and depth produce the same token, giving a structural (not textual) notion of coverage.
coverage_proxy.property: Rename-invariant: uses anon_method_index, not method name.

files.static_method: static int search(int[] arr, int target)
static void add(int), static boolean remove(int), static boolean contains(int)
files.stdin: one command per line: add X | remove X | contains X
files.stdout: true/false per remove or contains command

design_decisions.decision: String-level instrumentation, not ASM/Javassist bytecode instrumentation
design_decisions.rationale: Benchmark programs are simple (no nested classes, no lambdas in hot paths). String manipulation avoids a 3rd-party dependency and keeps the instrumenter auditable at a glance.
For benchmark programs, manual instrumentation is more readable and verifiable than auto-generated code. JavaInstrumenter.instrument() detects the TRACE ENTER marker and skips re-injection.

design_decisions.decision: stderr for trace output, stdout for functional output
design_decisions.rationale: Allows subprocess to capture both streams independently. Functional correctness can be checked from stdout; behavioral trace is read from stderr. No interleaving risk.
Without source line numbers, method-call depth encodes structural path information. Combining with anon_idx ensures two different methods at the same depth produce different tokens.
Ensures anon_call_freq keying is semantically equivalent between Python and Java genomes, making the distance() function meaningful across languages.

limitations: String-level instrumenter does not handle: nested anonymous classes, lambda expressions, multi-catch blocks, or programs with non-trivial generics in method signatures.
Coverage proxy (depth × anon_idx) is a structural approximation — not equivalent to Python's sys.settrace line coverage.
callDepth is a static field: not thread-safe. Acceptable for single-threaded benchmark programs.
Only 3 of the 10 cross-language pairs have Java implementations in this version.
future_work: Add Java files for p02 (insertion sort), p04–p10 to complete the 10-pair cross-language corpus.
Add cross-language distance() evaluation: run both Python and Java genomes through the existing DynamicGenome distance function, validate d < 0.3 for equivalent pairs.
Replace string-level instrumenter with a proper JavaParser-based instrumenter for richer programs.
